messages:
kevin_sales: Kicking off MerchantBridge POC — they want to swap from CompetitorX API. Main asks: prompt parity, tokenization/billing deltas, and data residency/SOC2. Can infra handle prefix caching for short chat sessions? cc @mae @eli @rachel_sec
mae: re: prefix caching — yes, runtime supports KV cache; we'll surface cache-hit rates in console. For prompt parity, need mapping for competitor params: temperature -> temp, top_p -> nucleus. They use 'stop_sequences' vs our 'stop' array. small difference.
eli: noted. Biggest risk is tokenization differences: CompetitorX counts tokens on utf-16 surrogate pairs differently; customers saw ~12% more tokens. We should run tokenization sandbox. Also their response envelope includes 'meta' field we don't — adapters needed.
rachel_sec: security Q: MerchantBridge requires on-prem option + dedicated KMS and signed attestations. I attached the questionnaire here: https://redwood-internal.s3/MB-SecQ-2024.pdf. @kevin_sales ask them to fill and return by EOD Friday.
kevin_sales: sending questionnaire now. Billing question from their finance: how to estimate per-conversation cost given batching & cache? @jonah can you provide the ballpark?
jonah: quick calc — assume avg conv = 6 turns, 350 tokens per convo, with 12% token uplift from tokenization delta = 392 tokens. Hosted rate $0.0006/token => ~ $0.235 per convo. Dedicated pricing: if commit 100k conv/mo, we can offer flat capacity + 20% discount; i'll post spreadsheet.
mae: for parity tests I propose 3 prompt buckets: (1) short chat (<=128 tokens), (2) structured completion (few-shot), (3) long context (>=2048). We'll run 500 samples each and record BLEU/ROUGE + qualitative evals.
eli: adapter plan: shim will rewrite stop_sequences -> stop, map 'max_tokens' -> 'max_new_tokens', and normalize response envelope. Example snippet:
```
// shim pseudocode
payload.prompt = req.prompt
payload.max_new_tokens = req.max_tokens
payload.stop = req.stop_sequences || req.stop
```
We should also add a 'compat_mode' flag to responses so they can fall back.
rachel_sec: legal asks about data residency — MerchantBridge needs EU-only storage and no logs retained >30d. For Private we can set retention and KMS in EU region. Need PO details.
kevin_sales: flagged enterprise blocker: they use IP allowlist + strict egress rules. Can we support static outbound IPs for Dedicated? @mae
mae: Dedicated supports static egress IPs when deployed in customer's VPC, yes. For Hosted we can provide region-specific egress but not static IP. I'll note deployment ops steps.
sre-bot: deploy-check: Dedicated pool capacity available in eu-west-1 for requested GPU 4xA10 — 3x nodes free. ETA for on-prem packaging: 10 business days.
jonah: Pricing follow-up: added a sample Excel to sales drive: https://drive.redwood/sales/merchantbridge-pricing.xlsx. Highlights: estimated TCO including canary + fallback is in tab 'Estimates'.
kevin_sales: next steps: 1) Send sec questionnaire (done), 2) run tokenization sandbox (eli/mae) — target Wed, 3) run parity evals (mae) — start Thu, 4) draft POC success criteria + pricing (jonah) — EOD Mon. @everyone ack.
eli: ack. I'll provision tokenization sandbox and drop curl examples.
mae: ack.
rachel_sec: ack, will review sec Q on receipt.
kevin_sales: thanks team :pray:
